title: Where do cashews grow in India?
description: Discover India's cashew-growing regions, why warm coastal climates suit kaju, and how soil, rainfall and local varieties shape the crop.
author: ZIVASHA Editorial
imageAlt: ZIVASHA dry-fruit gift presentation with four glass jars
imageCaption: ZIVASHA gift presentation. Background and branding edited; this image does not identify the origin of a particular batch.
intro: A cashew in a festive gift box has an agricultural story behind it. Known as kaju in many Indian households, cashew is a tropical crop whose growing regions reflect a useful combination of warmth, seasonal rain and freely draining soil.
takeaway: Warmth, good drainage and a distinct dry season help explain India's coastal cashew belt.

sections.heading: India's coastal cashew belt
paragraphs: On the west coast, cashews are cultivated in Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala. The eastern growing belt includes Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. ICAR also describes cultivation in parts of the North East, so the crop's Indian story extends beyond the familiar coastal states.

sections.heading: Why do these regions suit kaju?
paragraphs: Cashew trees favour tropical warmth; young plants are sensitive to frost. Cultivation guidance hosted by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University identifies deep, well-drained sandy loams as particularly suitable. Lateritic soils and slightly acidic coastal sands can also support the crop, while waterlogging is unsuitable.

Rain is only part of the story. A well-defined dry season helps flowering and fruiting. Excess rain and humidity during flowering can encourage disease and flower or fruit drop. These needs help explain the coastal connection, although suitability still depends on the orchard's soil, drainage and local weather.

sections.heading: One crop, many local varieties
paragraphs: Regional names offer another clue to India's cashew diversity: TNAU lists Vengurla varieties for Maharashtra, Ullal varieties for Karnataka and VRI varieties for Tamil Nadu. A variety name describes planting material; it should not be treated as proof of where a retail pack was grown.

sections.heading: What to ask when choosing a dry-fruit gift
paragraphs: Ask about the contents, net weight and batch origin if regional sourcing matters to you. This article describes general growing regions, not a claim that every ZIVASHA cashew comes from one particular state. For the contents and available pack options in our dry-fruit gift hampers, explore the collection or speak to our team.

title: What is Khapli wheat? A simple guide to emmer
description: Learn what Khapli wheat is, where emmer grows in India, how its husk differs from other wheat, and why Khapli atta and laddus contain gluten.
author: ZIVASHA Editorial
imageAlt: Illustrated ZIVASHA Khapli Laddu container presentation
imageCaption: AI-generated product illustration; actual appearance and packaging may vary. This image does not identify a farm or batch origin.
intro: Khapli wheat appears on atta packs and traditional sweet menus, but what does the name mean? Khapli refers to emmer wheat, also called Triticum dicoccum. Its identity, growing regions and gluten content are useful starting points when choosing Khapli atta or a sweet made with it.
takeaway: Khapli is emmer wheat, a hulled grain with a regional farming history. It contains gluten.

sections.heading: How is Khapli different from other wheat?
paragraphs: Agharkar Research Institute distinguishes Khapli from common bread wheat and durum wheat in its breeding programme. Emmer has long, slender kernels and is a hulled wheat: its husk remains attached during harvesting and must be removed during processing. The husk should not be confused with the edible grain inside.

sections.heading: Where does Khapli wheat grow in India?
paragraphs: Indian cultivation includes northern Karnataka, southern Maharashtra, coastal Gujarat and parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. ICAR–IARI describes emmer’s adaptation to marginal and stony soils and notes that the cool, temperate conditions of the Nilgiris suit its cultivation.

There is no single climate story for every Khapli field. Variety, sowing season, irrigation and local conditions matter. A familiar regional name on a pack is therefore not proof that its grain came from a particular state.

sections.heading: Is Khapli wheat gluten-free?
paragraphs: No. The US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases lists emmer among wheat types that naturally contain gluten. Descriptions such as “ancient grain” or “wholegrain” do not make it gluten-free. People with coeliac disease should not treat Khapli atta or Khapli laddus as a gluten-free alternative.

sections.heading: From Khapli wheat to Khapli Laddu
paragraphs: A grain’s name alone does not describe a finished laddu. ZIVASHA Khapli Laddu includes khapli wheat, nuts, ghee and jaggery. It contains wheat gluten, nuts and milk ingredients. Read the complete ingredient and allergen declaration before choosing a pack.

Our Khapli Laddu is offered in 250 g and 500 g containers. These are net pack weights, not guaranteed piece counts. For gifting, confirm the number of containers, required date and delivery pincode, along with storage and best-before details.
The farming regions described here explain the grain, not the origin of ZIVASHA’s particular batches. Ask our team for available batch information if regional sourcing matters to your purchase.

title: Gond Laddu: ingredients, edible gond and choosing a pack
description: What is Gond Laddu made of? Understand edible gond, ZIVASHA’s key ingredients, pack weights and the details to check before buying mithai gifts.

imageCaption: AI-generated product illustration; actual appearance and packaging may vary. The illustration does not identify the gum species or batch origin.
intro: Gond Laddu is an Indian sweet featuring edible gond. If you are choosing it for a gift, start with the ingredients and pack details rather than assuming every recipe is the same. ZIVASHA’s key ingredients are edible gond, nuts, coconut and jaggery.
takeaway: Choose Gond Laddu by its complete ingredient declaration, allergens and net weight. The name “gond” alone does not identify a particular botanical source.

sections.heading: What does edible gond mean?
paragraphs: Edible plant gums are a group of ingredients, not one interchangeable material. FAO/JECFA describes gum arabic, also called acacia gum, as dried exudate from certain Acacia species. FAO separately identifies tragacanth as a gum obtained from Astragalus shrubs.

These examples explain why the gum’s identity matters; they do not establish which species is used in ZIVASHA’s recipe. That detail needs confirmation from the product specification. A photograph or a general name cannot verify the source.

sections.heading: What is in the laddu?
paragraphs: Our product overview lists gond, nuts, coconut and jaggery. It is a starting point, rather than the complete ingredient list in order of quantity. Recipes can differ, so ask for the final declaration instead of assuming flour, ghee or particular nuts are present or absent.

Food labels distinguish ingredients from allergen information. FSSAI’s labelling guidance covers both: check the ingredient list and the separate allergen declaration, including any cross-contact information relevant to the recipient.

sections.heading: Choosing a Gond Laddu gift
paragraphs: ZIVASHA offers 250 g and 500 g containers. These figures describe the total net contents, not the number of laddus. If you are planning individual gifts or a shared box, confirm the piece count you need before ordering.

For a bulk enquiry, share the pack size, number of containers, delivery pincode and required date. Ask for storage instructions and the applicable best-before information with the final pack details. This helps you choose for the occasion without relying on a generic shelf-life promise.

title: Where do walnuts grow in India? Why hills suit akhrot
description: Explore India's walnut-growing regions, from Jammu and Kashmir to Arunachal Pradesh, and learn why winter chill, soil and spring weather matter for akhrot.
author: ZIVASHA Editorial
imageAlt: ZIVASHA four-jar dry-fruit gift presentation used as gifting context
imageCaption: ZIVASHA gift presentation, shown for context. Background and branding edited; the image does not identify walnut contents, a farm or batch origin. Confirm the contents of your selected hamper.
intro: Walnuts grown in India have a strong connection with the Himalayas. Known as akhrot in Hindi, the walnut is a temperate nut crop. Its growing regions tell a story about winter cold, suitable soil and the timing of spring weather—not simply how high a place is.
takeaway: India's walnut belt is centred on Jammu and Kashmir, with cultivation in Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh. Cold winters help, but late spring frost can harm flowers.

sections.heading: India's main walnut-growing regions
paragraphs: APEDA identifies Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh as the main Indian growing regions. Jammu and Kashmir has the largest share of the country's walnut area and production. Kashmir walnuts are therefore a familiar part of the crop's Indian story, but they are not its only regional identity.

sections.heading: Why do Himalayan conditions suit akhrot?
paragraphs: The National Horticulture Board's walnut guidance specifies a temperate climate and a chilling period of roughly 400–1,000 hours. This winter requirement helps explain the crop's association with cool hill regions. The guidance is a planning range, not a guarantee that every variety will thrive at every hill site.

More cold is not always better. A 2025 Indian Farming article explains that late spring frost can damage walnut flowers and sharply reduce yields. Winter chill and a damaging frost during flowering are different conditions: their timing matters.

sections.heading: Soil and water matter too
paragraphs: NHB lists loamy to clay-loam soils and a pH of 6–7 in its walnut guidance. It also recommends well-drained orchard sites to help manage root and crown rot, and identifies fruit development as a critical stage for water supply. A cold location alone is therefore not enough; the orchard needs suitable soil, drainage and water.

sections.heading: Growing regions are not proof of a pack's origin
paragraphs: A general guide to Indian agriculture cannot establish where a particular retail batch was grown. If origin matters to your purchase, request batch-specific sourcing information instead of relying on a regional name or photograph.

For a ZIVASHA dry-fruit gift, confirm the selected nuts and net weights before ordering; do not assume every hamper includes walnuts. Explore our gift collection and ask the team about the contents of your preferred pack.

title: Where does sesame grow in India? A guide to til
description: Discover where sesame grows in India, why warm weather and well-drained soil suit til, and how its growing season varies across regions.
author: ZIVASHA Editorial
imageAlt: Illustrated ZIVASHA Seven Seeds Nutri Bar presentation, shown as seed-based gifting context
imageCaption: AI-generated product illustration; actual appearance and packaging may vary. Shown as seed-based gifting context, not as proof of sesame content, a farm or batch origin. Confirm the complete ingredient list.
intro: Sesame, commonly called til or gingelly, is a tiny seed with a wide farming footprint. Where sesame grows in India depends on warmth, seasonal moisture and local cropping practices. Its story stretches across several regions rather than belonging to one state or one sowing season.
takeaway: Sesame grows across many Indian regions. Warm conditions suit it, while drainage and the timing of water supply matter as much as rainfall.

sections.heading: Where does sesame grow in India?
paragraphs: ICAR's sesame variety-testing zones illustrate this breadth. Its kharif zones include Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana; Madhya Pradesh and eastern states such as Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha; Gujarat, Maharashtra and Telangana; and southern states including Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Andhra Pradesh.
These are agricultural testing regions, not a ranking of today's largest producers. ICAR also separates summer and rabi sesame zones, showing why a single national crop calendar would be misleading.

sections.heading: Why warmth and well-drained soil suit til
paragraphs: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University describes sesame as a tropical crop and gives an optimum temperature range of 25–35°C. Warm growing conditions help explain its suitability across many Indian farming regions.

Drainage is equally important. NC State Extension's sesame research guidance warns that the crop is sensitive to waterlogging. A field that stays saturated after rain can be unsuitable even when its temperature is favourable.

sections.heading: The growing season changes with location
paragraphs: Tamil Nadu offers a useful example: TNAU lists February–March sowing for irrigated sesame in Coimbatore, Tiruppur and Erode, alongside June–July sowing for rainfed crops in the western zone. Local rainfall, irrigation and variety influence the choice.

Sesame's drought tolerance does not mean it needs no water. TNAU identifies flowering and pod setting among the important stages for irrigation. The timing of moisture matters, rather than simply the year's total rainfall.

sections.heading: From growing regions to a food gift
paragraphs: This guide describes sesame cultivation, not the sourcing or recipe of a particular ZIVASHA batch. For seed-based gifts, check the complete ingredients, allergens and net weight; a product name or illustration cannot confirm every seed used.
Explore ZIVASHA's Seven Seeds Nutri Bar page for pack information, and ask our team for the details relevant to your chosen gift.

title: Jaggery sweets: what does “No white sugar added” mean?
description: Understand jaggery sweets, no-white-sugar wording, total and added sugars, and the pack details to check when choosing laddus or seed bars.
author: ZIVASHA Editorial
imageAlt: Illustrated ZIVASHA Gond Laddu container presentation
imageCaption: AI-generated product illustration; actual appearance and packaging may vary. The illustration does not establish a serving size or nutrition value.
intro: When choosing jaggery sweets, “No white sugar added” tells you something specific about the recipe. It does not tell you how much total sugar is in a laddu or bar. Understanding that distinction makes product descriptions and nutrition information easier to read together.
takeaway: Jaggery contributes sugar. A recipe made without white sugar is not automatically sugar-free or made without added sugar.

sections.heading: Does jaggery count as sugar?
paragraphs: Yes. ICMR–National Institute of Nutrition includes jaggery among sugars added during food preparation. Replacing white sugar with jaggery changes the sweetening ingredient; it does not remove the sugars it contributes. “Sweetened with jaggery” describes an ingredient choice, rather than a promise of lower sugar or a health benefit.

sections.heading: Read total sugars and added sugars separately
paragraphs: Total sugars include naturally occurring sugars and any added sugars in the food. The US FDA explains this distinction in its consumer guide to nutrition labels. Do not add the two figures together as though they were separate totals.

When comparing packs, check whether the figures use the same basis, such as 100 g or a stated serving. A 250 g container describes pack weight, not one serving. Ask for the finished product’s nutrition declaration rather than estimating values from ingredient names.

sections.heading: What does ZIVASHA’s wording cover?
paragraphs: Gond Laddu, Khapli Laddu and Seven Seeds Nutri Bar are sweetened with jaggery, with no white sugar added. Gond Laddu and Seven Seeds Nutri Bar also contain dates.

These products still contain sugars. Ask for the complete ingredient list, allergens, serving information and nutrition declaration before choosing for a particular dietary need. Khapli contains wheat and gluten. A sweetener description alone cannot establish suitability for the recipient.

paragraphs: Check with your child’s school about food restrictions and its approach to allergies before selecting a snack. Do not assume every school has the same rules. intro: After a dry-fruit hamper is unwrapped, its food labels are still useful. Keep them with the jars or packs rather than discarding them with the decorative wrapping. The practical question is not simply how long dry fruits usually last, but how the food you received should be stored.
takeaway: Read each actual pack’s dates and storage instructions together, and check for separate directions after opening.

sections.heading: Read the date alongside the storage conditions
paragraphs: FSSAI’s Eat Right India guidance tells consumers to check manufacture and expiry or best-before dates, and read storage instructions covering where to keep a product and for how long. Check both parts of the label. A printed date should not be treated as a promise that food will keep under any conditions.

sections.heading: Check again when you open a pack
paragraphs: Look for instructions that apply after opening. NSW Food Authority explains that directions such as refrigeration or a stated period after opening need to be followed for the food to keep as intended. Those are examples, not universal instructions for every dry-fruit pack. Use the directions on your actual product; do not borrow a storage duration from another brand or assortment.

sections.heading: Pass the information on with the gift
paragraphs: If you separate jars for different recipients, keep the relevant food information with each one. If you move food into another container, retain its original label. Noting when you opened a pack can help you follow any after-opening instruction; it does not replace the printed date.

For a ZIVASHA selection, ask for the supplied batch’s date and storage details if anything is missing or unclear. A catalogue photograph cannot establish shelf life, and we do not assign one duration to every hamper.
